title: Calming George Whiting while writing the Guinan shows
summary: Johnson walked the hot-tempered Whiting outside during the Guinan shows and reminded him that Johnson was not in ASCAP.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Working with Sinatra: bands, Vegas and the Sands

blocks.x: .. but he was in New York and so was I, so we began to write songs together, and -- but later, George kind of quieted his temper down. I guess I helped him do it when we wrote the Gynam shows. Because he was -- he flared up a couple of times, and I had to take him outside and walk him a little bit like you would walk a dog, you know?

So I'd walk him and kind of stroke him right and tell him, you see, George, you're in ASCAP and you draw a nice, fat check every three months, and I'm not in ASCAP, George, and I don't draw a nice, fat check, and this money that I'm getting from here means a lot to me -- well, that always would bring him down -- which was the truth.

And then he'd apologize and it just wouldn't happen any more on that job, he just wouldn't do it -- he'd find himself getting angry and he'd get up and go out, but he wouldn't say anything. Not one word. So that came from his affection for me, and my affection for him -- I thought that -- well, I looked up to him, he was something. A guy who can write lyrics like "Molly and Me and Baby Makes Three" can't do any wrong lyrically.
But I guess maybe talking gets something stirred up in my throat instead of in my head.
